findings.title: Bash allow-listed without restriction
findings.rationale: `Bash`, `Bash(*)` or `Bash(*:*)` in permissions.allow lets the agent run any shell command without a prompt. Prompt injection in any file the agent reads becomes code execution.
findings.remediation: Allow specific commands, e.g. `Bash(git status:*)`, `Bash(npm test)`.

findings.title: Bash allow-list grants `sudo`
findings.rationale: A prefix rule for an interpreter (`python3 *`), a downloader (`curl *`), a privilege tool (`sudo *`) or a leading wildcard (`*foo*`) is equivalent to unrestricted execution.
findings.remediation: Remove `sudo` from the allow list; approve such commands interactively.

findings.title: Permission prompts bypassed by default
findings.rationale: `permissions.defaultMode` of `bypassPermissions`/`dontAsk`, `skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt`, or the Desktop bypass opt-in removes the human from every tool call.
findings.remediation: Use `default` or `acceptEdits`; enable bypass only for a sandboxed run.

findings.title: Hook downloads and executes remote code
findings.rationale: Hooks run on every matching tool call with the user's privileges. Their scripts are part of the trust boundary and should be reviewed like code.
findings.remediation: Vendor the script into the repository and run it from a fixed path.

findings.title: Credential stored in settings env (OpenAI-style key)
findings.rationale: `env` values are injected into every tool process and are easy to leak via `settings.json` backups, dotfile repositories and screenshots.
findings.remediation: Move the value to the OS keychain or an `apiKeyHelper`; reference it as `${VAR}`.

findings.title: Credential stored in settings env (secret-like key name)
findings.rationale: `env` values are injected into every tool process and are easy to leak via `settings.json` backups, dotfile repositories and screenshots.
findings.remediation: Move the value to the OS keychain or an `apiKeyHelper`; reference it as `${VAR}`.

findings.title: Credential stored in settings env (GitHub token)
findings.rationale: `env` values are injected into every tool process and are easy to leak via `settings.json` backups, dotfile repositories and screenshots.
findings.remediation: Move the value to the OS keychain or an `apiKeyHelper`; reference it as `${VAR}`.

findings.title: Bash allow-list grants arbitrary `python3` execution
findings.rationale: A prefix rule for an interpreter (`python3 *`), a downloader (`curl *`), a privilege tool (`sudo *`) or a leading wildcard (`*foo*`) is equivalent to unrestricted execution.
findings.remediation: Allow only the exact scripts you run, e.g. `Bash(python3 scripts/build.py)`.

findings.title: Bash allow-list grants arbitrary `python3` execution
findings.rationale: A prefix rule for an interpreter (`python3 *`), a downloader (`curl *`), a privilege tool (`sudo *`) or a leading wildcard (`*foo*`) is equivalent to unrestricted execution.
findings.remediation: Allow only the exact scripts you run, e.g. `Bash(python3 scripts/build.py)`.

findings.title: Bash allow-list grants unrestricted `curl` (network egress)
findings.rationale: A prefix rule for an interpreter (`python3 *`), a downloader (`curl *`), a privilege tool (`sudo *`) or a leading wildcard (`*foo*`) is equivalent to unrestricted execution.
findings.remediation: Restrict to known hosts or approve network commands interactively.

findings.title: Bash allow-list entry starts with a wildcard
findings.rationale: A prefix rule for an interpreter (`python3 *`), a downloader (`curl *`), a privilege tool (`sudo *`) or a leading wildcard (`*foo*`) is equivalent to unrestricted execution.
findings.remediation: Anchor the pattern to a command name; a leading `*` matches any command.

findings.title: Hook runs unpinned package `some-hook-linter` on every PreToolUse
findings.rationale: Hooks run on every matching tool call with the user's privileges. Their scripts are part of the trust boundary and should be reviewed like code.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version or install the tool once and call the binary.

findings.title: Project MCP servers auto-approved
findings.rationale: `enableAllProjectMcpServers: true` starts every server declared in a repository's `.mcp.json` without asking. Cloning a malicious repository then runs its servers.
findings.remediation: Set to false and approve project servers one by one.

findings.title: Additional directory grants whole-filesystem or home access
findings.rationale: `permissions.additionalDirectories` widens the agent's file scope; `/` or the home directory defeats project isolation (SSH keys, browser profiles, other repositories).
findings.remediation: List only the specific directories the task needs.

findings.title: Sandbox disabled
findings.rationale: With `sandbox.enabled: false`, shell commands run with the full privileges of the user instead of inside the OS sandbox, so a permission mistake has no second barrier.
findings.remediation: Enable the sandbox and add explicit exceptions where a tool needs them.

findings.title: Lifecycle hook executes a shell command
findings.rationale: Hooks run on every matching tool call with the user's privileges. Their scripts are part of the trust boundary and should be reviewed like code.
findings.remediation: Review the script run on `PreToolUse`; keep it in version control.
